tagline: Down the Delta, with the river levee off one shoulder.
intro: From the Helena Bridge the road comes into Mississippi on US 49, turns south on Highway 1 as far as Onward, then follows US 61 to the Warren County line above Vicksburg, about 175 miles in all. Along much of the way the levee stands behind the fields and hides the river. Men with buckets, shovels and mules built it.

The country is flat enough to see the horizon over both shoulders, laid down by floods as topsoil more than 100 feet deep in places. The fields go from green wheat in early spring to white cotton in early fall.

moments.title: Friars Point
moments.text: Jesse James came through one evening in the 1880s, called on the Methodist minister, played poker at the saloon, and was gone by morning.

moments.title: Rosedale
moments.text: Locals hold that Robert Johnson sold his soul to the Devil where Highways 1 and 8 meet at the south end of town, though other Delta towns claim the same deal.

moments.title: Onward
moments.text: A state marker at the Onward Store recalls the 1902 hunt nearby when Theodore Roosevelt would not shoot a bear his guide Holt Collier had tied to a tree, and the Teddy Bear followed.

sources.label: MDOT, Mississippi Delta Great River Road Corridor Management Plan
